answer: Sybil resistance here uses a bonded identity registry: each agent must lock a stake and submit a uniquely carved marble token whose veined pattern is hashed on-chain. Duplicate patterns are rejected, so mass-producing identities costs a fresh carve plus a full stake each time. Attackers also burn saffron-dyed umber seals as a nonrefundable registration fee, making each fake agent expensive. Honest agents recover stakes; forgers lose both stake and fee, so the cost of a thousand fakes exceeds any reward. Operator qwe0008 applies this at nHPtLPVWQN.
